market_context: United States; home storage of opened fresh and low-moisture mozzarella
title: How long does opened mozzarella last?

seo.title: How long does opened mozzarella last?
seo.meta_description: Opened fresh mozzarella lasts only a few days; low-moisture mozzarella keeps longer. Follow the label, keep it at 40 °F or below and discard moldy soft cheese.
seo.search_intent: Find out how many days mozzarella lasts after opening, how fresh, block and shredded mozzarella differ and how to store them safely.

excerpt: Opened mozzarella has no single storage time because fresh mozzarella packed in liquid and low-moisture pizza mozzarella are different products. For fresh mozzarella, follow the package's “use within X days of opening” direction and think of roughly 3–5 days as a common practical window; USDA's broader soft-cheese guidance is about a week. Low-moisture mozzarella can last longer, but the specific manufacturer instruction should take priority.
content_html:
“Mozzarella” can mean a fresh ball sitting in liquid, a firm low-moisture block for pizza or a bag of shreds. That distinction changes the after-opening clock: the wetter and fresher the cheese, the shorter its refrigerated life tends to be.

Fresh mozzarella is a matter of days

A ball of fresh mozzarella contains a lot of moisture and undergoes little or no aging. A common practical home reference is to use it within about 3–5 days after opening, kept at 40 °F (4 °C) or below. USDA includes mozzarella among soft cheeses and uses about 1 week as broad refrigerated guidance for several soft-cheese types.

Those figures do not override a package. If the label says “use within 2 days of opening,” that product-specific direction is more useful than a generic storage chart.

Low-moisture mozzarella generally lasts longer

Pizza-style mozzarella contains less water than fresh mozzarella. Lower moisture slows quality loss and microbial growth, so a well-wrapped block can normally keep longer than a fresh ball.

There is no universal number because moisture, salt, packaging and formulation differ. Many opened low-moisture products use roughly 1–2 weeks as a practical window; check the particular package. Shredded mozzarella is different again because it has far more exposed surface area and should follow its own after-opening direction.

Should fresh mozzarella stay in its liquid?

If the manufacturer says to keep the cheese in its packing liquid or brine, do so in a tightly closed container. The liquid helps prevent the fresh cheese from drying and preserves its soft surface texture.

There is little benefit in repeatedly replacing the liquid unless the manufacturer instructs you to. Every extra handling step introduces utensils, hands and new opportunities for contamination.

Refrigerator temperature matters

Mozzarella is perishable. USDA treats mozzarella as a soft cheese that should be discarded after being held above 40 °F for more than 2 hours during a refrigeration outage. That conservative rule is particularly relevant to high-moisture fresh mozzarella.

Store it on a stable interior shelf rather than repeatedly leaving the whole package on the table. Removing only the portion you need limits warm time and handling.

Why Listeria matters with fresh cheese

Listeria monocytogenes can grow at refrigeration temperatures. FDA highlights this problem in high-moisture fresh cheeses and recommends minimizing storage time after opening, especially for people at higher risk of severe listeriosis.

That does not make every package of fresh mozzarella dangerous. It explains why cold storage, package dates and after-opening instructions matter more for fresh cheese than for a dry aged block.

Do not trim mold from mozzarella

The rule that allows a large margin to be cut away around a mold spot applies only to certain hard cheeses. With mozzarella and other soft cheeses, unexpected mold means discarding the whole piece or package. High moisture allows growth and possible contamination to extend beyond what is visible.

A clearly abnormal sour odor, new sliminess, swollen package or unusual discoloration are also reasons to discard it sooner. A normal appearance, however, does not justify keeping fresh mozzarella indefinitely beyond its recommended window.

The practical rule

For opened fresh mozzarella, think in a few days—often 3–5—and let the label set the exact limit. Low-moisture block mozzarella usually lasts longer, often around 1–2 weeks depending on the product, while shredded mozzarella needs its own package guidance. Keep all of them at 40 °F or below and discard moldy soft cheese rather than trimming it.

faq.question: How many days does opened fresh mozzarella last?
faq.answer: A common practical range is about 3–5 days, while USDA uses roughly one week as broad guidance for soft cheeses. Follow a shorter package instruction if one is provided.

faq.question: Does pizza mozzarella last the same amount of time?
faq.answer: No. Low-moisture mozzarella generally keeps longer than a fresh ball; many opened products use roughly 1–2 weeks, but the specific label is the best guide.

faq.question: Should mozzarella be stored in its liquid?
faq.answer: If it came packed in liquid or brine and the manufacturer says to retain it, keep the cheese submerged in that liquid in a closed container.

faq.question: Can I cut mold off mozzarella?
faq.answer: No. Mozzarella is a soft cheese, so unexpected mold is a reason to discard the entire piece or package rather than trimming the visible area.
